name: Microsoft 365
contracting_entity: Microsoft Corporation (EU/UK contracts via Microsoft Ireland Operations Limited)
storage: UK data centres for tenants signed up in the UK; EU data centres for tenants signed up in the EU. Covers Exchange mail, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams chat and Copilot.
plans: All commercial plans, including Business Basic and Business Standard, based on the country chosen at sign-up
ai_detail: Microsoft states prompts, responses and data accessed through Microsoft Graph are not used to train foundation LLMs, including those used by Copilot. This applies to Copilot Chat included with business plans and paid Microsoft 365 Copilot.
nonprofit_offer: Microsoft 365 Business Basic grant for up to 300 users free, plus up to 75% off Business Standard and Business Premium. The free Business Premium grant ended from 1 July 2025.
note: Your data stays in the UK or EU only if the tenant was set up with a UK or EU country, so check the data location in the admin centre. If you had the free Business Premium grant, check you moved users before it expired, or you risk losing data.

name: Google Workspace
contracting_entity: Google LLC (EMEA customers usually contract with Google Cloud EMEA Limited, Ireland)
storage: No location commitment by default. Business Standard and above can set a data region policy to Europe (EU); Business Starter and the free Nonprofits edition cannot. There is no UK-only region.
plans: Business Standard, Business Plus, Enterprise Standard and Plus (EU region via admin setting). Not Business Starter or the free Google Workspace for Nonprofits edition.
ai_detail: Google states Workspace does not use customer data to train models without the customer's prior permission or instruction. The Privacy Hub refers to qualifying editions and does not list Business Starter or Nonprofits separately.
nonprofit_offer: Google Workspace for Nonprofits edition free; Business Standard about USD 3.50 per user per month and Business Plus about USD 6.16 (annual), through Google for Nonprofits.
note: On the free Nonprofits edition or Business Starter you cannot choose where your data is stored. To keep data in Europe you need Business Standard or higher and must set the data region to Europe yourself.

name: Dropbox
contracting_entity: Dropbox, Inc. (outside North America: Dropbox International Unlimited Company, Ireland)
storage: US data centres by default. Teams can ask to move data to the UK or EU if they meet conditions.
plans: Standard, Advanced, Business, Business Plus or Enterprise teams with at least 10 licences on annual billing; requests reviewed individually
ai_detail: Dropbox says it will not build generative AI models using customer content without consent. Dash uses OpenAI for web search, on by default in chats, and says data sent is not used to train OpenAI models.
nonprofit_offer: 40% off Business Standard and Advanced through TechSoup (announced 2020, for US 501(c)(3) organisations). Availability for UK charities: unknown.
note: Your files are stored in the US unless your team has at least 10 licences on annual billing and asks Dropbox to move them. Small teams should assume US storage.

name: IONOS Nextcloud Workspace
contracting_entity: IONOS SE (UK customers contract with IONOS Cloud UK Limited)
storage: IONOS data centres in Germany
plans: All plans
ai_detail: The AI assistant runs on the IONOS AI Model Hub. IONOS says it contractually guarantees company data will never be used to train public AI models.
note: Your data is held in Germany and the software is open source, so you can move to another Nextcloud host. The UK contract is with IONOS Cloud UK Limited, so check which entity is on your agreement.

name: Hetzner Storage Share
storage: Hetzner's own data centre in Falkenstein, Germany. No other location offered.
plans: All plans (NX11, NX21, NX31)
ai_detail: Hetzner's Storage Share pages advertise no AI features. Any AI apps would be ones you install yourself from the Nextcloud app store.
note: Files are stored in Germany and are not encrypted by default. Hetzner's docs do not mention two-factor login, so check you can switch it on for every user.

name: mailbox.org
storage: Own servers in data centres in Berlin, Germany
plans: All plans
ai_detail: No AI features are listed on mailbox.org's plans or product pages.
note: Mail, calendars and files are stored in Berlin and use open standards, so moving out is straightforward. The service rebranded from mailbox.org to mailbox in September 2025, so look for either name on invoices.

name: Proton
storage: Switzerland primarily. Proton says business data is on servers in Europe under Swiss law. Some infrastructure has been moved to Germany and Norway since 2024 to 2025, but no customer choice of location is stated.
ai_detail: Proton says Proton Scribe does not use content data to train its models, and Lumo keeps no server-side logs and uses zero-access encryption. Scribe is an add-on; Lumo is included in Workspace Premium.
nonprofit_offer: Discount for registered nonprofits on business plans, amount agreed with sales on request.
note: Data is mainly held in Switzerland, which is outside the UK and EU but has UK and EU adequacy decisions. Most content is end-to-end encrypted, so if you lose your password and recovery details, the data cannot be recovered.

name: Infomaniak kSuite
storage: Infomaniak's own data centres in Switzerland
plans: Unknown.
ai_detail: Infomaniak says data sent to its Euria assistant is neither saved nor used to train AI, and processing stays in its Swiss data centres. Euria runs on open source models.
nonprofit_offer: Unknown.
note: Your data is held in Switzerland, which is outside the UK and EU but has UK and EU adequacy decisions. You can take your data out in standard formats: files over WebDAV, mail over IMAP, contacts as vCard and calendars as ICS. Two-step login is an Infomaniak account setting, so check it is switched on for every staff account. Nonprofit pricing: unknown, so ask Infomaniak.

name: Tuta
storage: Tuta's own servers in ISO 27001 certified data centres in Germany
plans: All plans
ai_detail: No AI features are listed on Tuta's business or security pages.
nonprofit_offer: 50% off for registered nonprofits and schools, by emailing sales with proof of status.
note: Data is stored in Germany and is end-to-end encrypted. You cannot connect ordinary email apps over IMAP, so exporting mail means using Tuta's desktop app.

name: Zoom
storage: Plan assumed: Zoom Workplace Pro. Recordings, transcripts and other customer content are stored in the US by default. Admins on paid plans, including Pro, can move recordings, transcripts, in-meeting chat and whiteboards to Germany, but account and operational data stay in the US.
plans: Paid plans including Pro can set the storage region to Germany for recordings, transcripts, in-meeting chat and whiteboard content. Zoom's fuller EU infrastructure is described for EU Education and Enterprise customers. No UK storage region is listed.
ai_detail: Zoom's terms (section 10.2) say it does not use audio, video, chat, screen sharing, attachments or other communications-like content to train Zoom or third-party AI models. This applies to all plans; no opt-out is needed.
nonprofit_offer: 50% off Zoom Workplace Pro and Business, the Large Meeting add-on and Zoom Webinar for verified nonprofits with budgets under US$10 million, verified through Goodstack. No longer offered through TechSoup.
note: Recordings are stored in the US unless an admin changes the data storage location to Germany in account settings. Account data stays in the US either way.

name: Microsoft Teams
storage: Plan assumed: Microsoft 365 Business Basic (nonprofit grant) or Business Standard. For a tenant whose default geography is the UK, Teams chats are stored at rest in the UK under Microsoft's Product Terms. EU tenants get EU storage. Meeting recordings are saved to the recorder's OneDrive, which follows the same data residency rules.
plans: All commercial Microsoft 365 plans that include Teams, based on the tenant's default geography (UK or EU). Advanced Data Residency is a paid add-on for stronger commitments.
ai_detail: Microsoft states that prompts, responses and data accessed through Microsoft Graph are not used to train foundation large language models, including those used by Copilot. Optional feedback may be used to improve the service.
nonprofit_offer: Microsoft 365 Business Basic grant for up to 300 users, and up to 75% off Business Standard and Business Premium. The free Business Premium and Office 365 E1 grants ended for new grants on 1 July 2025.
note: For UK tenants, Teams chats are stored in the UK. Recordings are saved in the OneDrive of the person who pressed record, so check where they end up when that person leaves.

name: Slack
storage: Plan assumed: Pro (free for nonprofits with up to 250 members). Data is stored in the US. Business+ and Enterprise plans can choose data residency in London, Frankfurt, Paris, Stockholm or Zurich, but member profiles, membership details and analytics stay outside the chosen region.
plans: Business+ and Enterprise (London, Frankfurt, Paris, Stockholm, Zurich). Not available on Free or Pro.
ai_detail: Slack analyses customer data (messages, content, files) to train non-generative global models, such as emoji and channel recommendations, on all plans by default. Workspace owners can opt out by emailing feedback@slack.com with the subject 'Slack Global model opt-out request'. Slack says it does not train generative AI models on customer data without opt-in consent.
nonprofit_offer: Free Pro plan for workspaces with 250 or fewer members, 85% off Pro above that, and 85% off Business+. Eligibility checked through TechSoup.
note: On Pro, messages are stored in the US and private channels and DMs cannot be exported. Slack uses your data for its recommendation models unless an owner emails feedback@slack.com to opt out.

name: WhatsApp (work groups)
contracting_entity: WhatsApp LLC (UK users); WhatsApp Ireland Limited (EEA users)
storage: Plan assumed: free personal WhatsApp accounts used for work groups. Messages are end-to-end encrypted and stored on each member's phone. WhatsApp keeps undelivered messages and media encrypted on its servers for up to 30 days. Other account data is shared globally within Meta, including the US. No UK or EU storage option exists.
ai_detail: Ordinary messages are end-to-end encrypted and are not used to train Meta AI. Anything sent to Meta AI, including when someone types @Meta AI in a group, is not end-to-end encrypted and can be used under Meta's privacy policy. Advanced Chat Privacy, off by default, disables some Meta AI features in a chat.
note: Work messages live on staff and volunteers' own phones, so the charity has no central copy and cannot control what leaves with them. Anyone typing @Meta AI in a group sends that part of the chat to Meta unencrypted.

name: WhatsApp Business app
contracting_entity: WhatsApp LLC (UK users); WhatsApp Ireland Limited (EEA users)
storage: Plan assumed: the free WhatsApp Business app (not the paid Business Platform API). Chats are stored on the phone the business number is registered on. Other data is shared globally within Meta, including the US. No UK or EU storage option exists.
ai_detail: Messages are end-to-end encrypted and not used to train Meta AI. Any AI tools the business connects are governed by their own terms. Messages sent to Meta AI are not end-to-end encrypted.
note: The app is tied to one phone number and one phone, so decide who holds that phone and how chats are kept when staff change. UK accounts are provided by WhatsApp LLC in the US.

name: Signal
storage: Plan assumed: the free Signal app. Messages are end-to-end encrypted and stored on members' devices. Signal's servers only queue encrypted messages for offline devices. Its terms say encrypted information and metadata are transferred to the US and other countries. Signal says it can only provide a user's registration date and last connection date.
ai_detail: Signal cannot read message content, which is end-to-end encrypted, and offers no AI features that use it.
note: Signal holds almost no data about you, but the charity has no admin controls or central copy of chats. Switch on Registration Lock with a PIN to stop someone taking over an account.

name: Element (hosted)
storage: Plan assumed: an Element-hosted server (Element Matrix Services / Element Cloud). Element hosts on Amazon Web Services, with its admin server in Amsterdam and deployment server in Stockholm. Customers choose the location of their own server when they set it up; the list of locations is not published.
plans: Location is chosen at set-up for hosted servers. Element's current public pricing page lists only self-hosted plans (Community free for up to 100 users; Enterprise from 100 users), so the small-organisation hosted offer is unclear.
ai_detail: Element's privacy policy does not mention AI or machine learning training. It says nobody at Element or its processors can access encrypted data.
note: Check which hosting location was picked when your server was set up, and use your own domain so you can move later. Element's published prices now focus on self-hosting.

name: Jitsi Meet (meet.jit.si)
storage: Plan assumed: the free public service at meet.jit.si. 8x8 does not say where its servers are. Chat is only kept during the meeting, recordings are held for up to 24 hours until uploaded to your Dropbox, and audio and video are not stored. 8x8 stores the account that created each room.
ai_detail: The meet.jit.si privacy supplement (last updated August 2023) does not mention AI. It says 8x8 uses personal information to deliver and improve the service.
nonprofit_offer: Free to use.
note: meet.jit.si is free and keeps little meeting content, but 8x8 does not say where its servers are. Since August 2023 whoever starts a meeting must sign in with Google, GitHub or Facebook.

name: Mattermost Cloud
storage: Plan assumed: Mattermost Cloud, which is now sold only through Mattermost sales as an annual subscription with a 100-user minimum. Cloud data, including messages, files, logs and backups, is stored in AWS us-east-1 in Virginia, US.
plans: No published EU or UK region. Mattermost says to contact its sales team or a partner for residency outside the US, or to self-host.
ai_detail: Mattermost's AI Agents connect to a language model provider that the admin configures. Whether Mattermost trains models on customer data: unknown.
nonprofit_offer: Nonprofit licence: 3 years of self-hosted Mattermost Professional for up to 1,000 users for US$250. Larger nonprofits are reviewed case by case, including for Cloud.
note: Mattermost Cloud is hosted in the US and needs at least 100 paid users. The nonprofit licence covers self-hosting, which puts the data wherever you host it.

name: Calendly
storage: US. Calendly says it stores user and invitee data in US data centres run by Google Cloud and Amazon Web Services, on all plans.
plans: Plan assumed: all plans (Free, Standard, Teams). Calendly's help page says the storage statement applies to all plans.
ai_detail: Calendly's security page says: 'Calendly does not sell customer data or use customer data to train AI models. Third-party AI providers are prohibited from using customer data to train their models.' Checked 29 September 2026.
nonprofit_offer: Unknown. Calendly's pricing page only says to contact sales about not-for-profit pricing.
note: Calendly holds your bookings and your invitees' details in the US, so tell people who book with you. You can export your meetings and your contacts as CSV files, but Calendly's help pages do not describe a single full export, so check what you need is covered. Two-factor login is available on all plans, so switch it on for every account. Calendly's pricing page only says to contact sales about not-for-profit pricing, so ask before you assume a discount.

name: ChatGPT
storage: Not stored in the UK or EU by default. Personal plans and ChatGPT Business have no data residency option. ChatGPT Enterprise and Edu customers can choose to store content at rest in Europe or the UK.
plans: ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Edu and eligible API customers (Europe and UK storage at rest; expanded to more regions in November 2025). Not ChatGPT Business, Free or Plus.
ai_detail: Free, Go, Plus and Pro (personal): chats are used to train models by default. Opt out by turning off 'Improve the model for everyone' in Settings > Data controls, or via the OpenAI Privacy Portal ('Do not train on my content'). Giving thumbs up or down feedback can still send that whole conversation for training. ChatGPT Business (formerly Team), Enterprise, Edu and the API: not used for training by default; an organisation can opt in.
nonprofit_offer: OpenAI for Nonprofits: ChatGPT Business Standard seats at $8 per user per month (annual) or $10 (monthly) after Goodstack verification; up to 75% off Enterprise for larger nonprofits via sales.
note: Personal ChatGPT accounts train on your chats unless each person turns this off, so staff should not use personal accounts for charity work. ChatGPT Business does not train on your data but stores it outside the UK and EU; only Enterprise offers UK or European storage.

name: Claude
storage: Stored in the US on all Claude plans. Processing may be routed to the US, Europe, Asia and Australia. No UK or EU storage option for Claude Team or Enterprise.
ai_detail: Free, Pro and Max (consumer): since 28 August 2025 each user chooses whether chats and coding sessions are used for training; existing users had to decide by 8 October 2025. If allowed, data is kept for up to five years; if not, the usual 30-day retention applies. Change it any time in Settings > Privacy (model improvement setting); incognito chats are never used. Team, Enterprise, API, Government and Education: not used for training by default.
nonprofit_offer: Claude for Nonprofits: Team plan at $8 per user per month and Enterprise at $10, verified through Goodstack; Anthropic's page lists US 501(c)(3) organisations as eligible, so check whether UK or EU charities qualify.
note: Personal Claude accounts may use chats for training if the person allowed it in the 2025 privacy prompt, so check Settings > Privacy. All Claude data is stored in the US, with no UK or EU storage option on any plan.

name: Google Gemini
storage: Not stated for personal accounts or ordinary Workspace plans. Workspace admins can keep Gemini data in the EU only on Enterprise Plus, Frontline Plus, Education editions or Assured Controls add-ons. The UK is not offered as a separate region.
plans: Workspace Enterprise Plus and Frontline Plus (EU processing and storage), Education Standard and Plus (EU storage only), Assured Controls add-ons. Not Workspace for Nonprofits, Business Starter or personal accounts.
ai_detail: Personal Google account (Gemini app): with Keep Activity on, which is the default, chats and uploads are used to improve Google's services, including training generative AI models, and a subset is reviewed by humans (kept up to 3 years, detached from the account). Turn off Keep Activity or use Temporary chats; chats are then kept for 72 hours and not used for training, unless you send feedback. Gemini in Google Workspace (work or school account): customer data is not used to train models without permission and is not human reviewed.
nonprofit_offer: Google for Nonprofits: Gemini app and Gemini Notebook are included in the no-cost Google Workspace for Nonprofits plan, with up to 75% off advanced Workspace editions for eligible nonprofits.
note: Staff using Gemini on personal Google accounts have their chats used for training and possibly read by reviewers unless they turn off Keep Activity. Use Gemini through the charity's Workspace account, where your data is not used for training.

name: Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat
storage: Prompts and responses are stored in the organisation's Microsoft 365 tenant (Exchange), so they follow the tenant's data location. EU tenants are covered by the EU Data Boundary, with exceptions. UK in-country processing was promised from late 2025, later adjusted to the end of 2026.
plans: Any Microsoft 365 work or school tenant located in the UK or EU, including Copilot Chat included with Microsoft 365 subscriptions.
ai_detail: For work or school (Entra ID) accounts, prompts, responses and data accessed through Microsoft Graph are not used to train foundation models, in both Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat with enterprise data protection (green shield). This does not cover the consumer Microsoft Copilot app used with a personal Microsoft account.
nonprofit_offer: Copilot Chat is included at no extra cost with eligible Microsoft 365 subscriptions, including nonprofit plans (Business Basic grant for up to 300 users; Business Premium at $5.50 per user per month). Microsoft's nonprofit pricing page lists no separate nonprofit price for Microsoft 365 Copilot Business.
note: Since 17 April 2026 Microsoft can process EU tenants' Copilot requests outside the EU at busy times (flex routing) unless an admin turns this off. Anthropic models and Bing web search in Copilot also sit outside the EU Data Boundary, so check these settings in the Microsoft 365 admin centre.

name: Mistral Vibe (was Le Chat)
storage: Hosted in the EU by default. Some features may transfer data temporarily outside the EU to listed subprocessors; Enterprise customers can switch some of those features off.
plans: All plans
ai_detail: Free: chats are used for training by default; opt out in the admin or privacy settings ('Allow your interactions to be used to train our models') or in the mobile app under Data & Account Controls. Pro: Mistral's pages conflict (the help centre says users are not opted out by default, the product docs say Pro is not trained on by default), so check the toggle. Team: admins can switch training off for the whole organisation; the docs say it is off by default. Enterprise: opted out by default. Thumbs up or down feedback can be used for training on any plan.
note: Le Chat was renamed Vibe on 12 August 2026; accounts and data carried over. Data is hosted in the EU, but check the training toggle in the admin panel, especially on Free and Pro.

name: Otter.ai
storage: US by default. Otter uses Amazon Web Services in the United States and relies on the Data Privacy Framework and Standard Contractual Clauses for UK and EU transfers. Otter does not list a UK or EU storage option.
ai_detail: Otter trains its own AI on de-identified audio recordings and on transcripts, which may contain personal information, on all plans. Human review of recordings for training needs the user's permission, which can be changed in account settings. Only Enterprise customers can also opt out of the de-identified data use.
note: Otter trains its AI on de-identified recordings and transcripts of your meetings, and only Enterprise customers can opt out. Data is stored in the US.

name: Fireflies.ai
storage: Stored on servers in the United States and other countries. Enterprise customers can buy private storage at a location they choose.
plans: Enterprise (private storage)
ai_detail: Fireflies says it does not use personal information or meeting content for AI model training and contractually bars its AI vendors from training on it, with zero data retention at those vendors. Applies to all plans.
note: Fireflies does not train AI on your meetings, but recordings and transcripts are stored in the US unless you pay for Enterprise private storage. Tell meeting guests the notetaker is recording.

name: Zoom AI Companion
storage: Follows the region the Zoom account is hosted in. Hosting region for new UK or EU accounts: unknown. Admins on Pro and above can choose Germany for recordings and some content, but out-of-meeting chat and account data stay in the provisioned region. The UK is not in the storage list.
plans: Pro and above can pick Germany for recordings, transcripts and some content; accounts hosted in the EU use Zoom-managed models (ZM+) to respect data residency.
ai_detail: Zoom says it does not use audio, video, chat, screen sharing, attachments or other communications-like content to train its own or third-party AI models. For US-hosted accounts AI Companion sends content to third-party models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) under zero data retention terms; admins can ask Zoom Support for Zoom-hosted-only processing (ZMO).
nonprofit_offer: Zoom gives 50% off Workplace Pro and Business annual plans to verified nonprofits (US 501(c)(3) or an international equivalent recognised by the regulator, operating budget of $10 million or less), verified through Goodstack. Whether this covers AI Companion on its own: unknown.
note: Zoom does not train AI on your meeting content, but by default AI Companion may send it to third-party AI providers for processing. Ask Zoom which region your account is hosted in and which AI processing option applies.

name: Mailchimp
contracting_entity: The Rocket Science Group LLC (Intuit Mailchimp)
storage: US by default for all customers (assumed plan: Essentials or Standard). No EU or UK hosting option. Transfers rely on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework and UK Extension, with SCCs as fallback.
ai_detail: Terms section 30 lets Mailchimp use generative AI Inputs and Outputs, including Customer Data, for machine learning to develop the AI model and services. Section 17 lets it aggregate and anonymise campaign content for its own use. The terms point to data preferences in account settings but do not describe a full opt-out.
nonprofit_offer: 15% off marketing plans. Non-US nonprofits can apply with their website; request before buying, as it is not applied retroactively.
note: Supporter data is stored in the US and there is no UK or EU hosting option. Check the data preferences in your account settings if you use the AI writing features.

name: Brevo
storage: EU for all customers (assumed plan: Starter). Hosted with OVH in France and Germany and Google Cloud in Belgium.
plans: All plans
ai_detail: Terms allow Brevo to use Content and Usage Data to train its AI features, limited to improving the services, in particular fraud, phishing and spam prevention and security. Other AI features can be managed in the Control Center, but fraud and spam detection cannot be switched off. Third-party AI providers only process data to provide the feature.
nonprofit_offer: 20% off any paid monthly or yearly plan for verified nonprofits; contact support with proof of status.
note: Data is held in the EU by default. Brevo can use your content to train its anti-spam and fraud AI, and that cannot be switched off.

name: CleverReach
storage: Germany and the EU for all customers (assumed plan: Basic). The supplier says servers are exclusively in Germany and the EU.
plans: All plans
ai_detail: The AI Content Generator sends your prompt to OpenAI. CleverReach does not say whether prompts are used for training or where OpenAI processes them. It is an optional feature on Basic and above. Training with recipient data: unknown.
nonprofit_offer: Discount for nonprofits on request; amount not published.
note: Recipient data stays in Germany and the EU. Full two-factor login is listed only on Enterprise; smaller plans can switch on an emailed PIN code at login under Settings.

name: Beacon CRM
storage: UK by default (assumed plan: Starter). Trust page says data is hosted exclusively in the UK on AWS; the sub-processor list names AWS London and Ireland and Google Cloud London for core storage.
plans: All plans
ai_detail: Beacon says Beacon AI cannot access your data and does not use it to train public AI models. The AI provider behind Beacon AI is not named in the sub-processor list.
note: Data is held in the UK. In late July 2026 attackers copied Beacon's customer database backups, affecting over 1,000 charities, so check what Beacon has told you and whether you have acted on it.

name: Salesforce Nonprofit
storage: Depends on the region the org is provisioned in (assumed plan: Power of Us donated Enterprise Edition). Hyperforce runs in the UK, Germany and other countries, and data is generally stored in the country where the org is located. The Hyperforce EU Operating Zone adds stronger EU and Swiss residency commitments but is not offered for the UK. Generative AI features may route data to LLM providers such as OpenAI or Azure.
plans: Hyperforce orgs provisioned in a UK or EU region; EU Operating Zone for EU and Swiss customers
ai_detail: Salesforce says generative AI features are not trained on customer data, but predictive Einstein features can use org data for global models. Since the Spring 2026 release admins can switch this off under Setup > Opt Out of Customer Data Access; most orgs start opted in.
nonprofit_offer: Power of Us programme: 10 donated Enterprise Edition licences of Agentforce Nonprofit (or Sales and Service Cloud) for eligible nonprofits.
note: Check your instance location on my.trust.salesforce.com, because storage depends on where your org was set up. Ask your admin to review the Opt Out of Customer Data Access setting, which starts switched to allow data use.

name: CiviCRM
storage: Depends entirely on the host (assumed: hosted by a CiviCRM partner). Self-hosted or partner-hosted data sits wherever that server is. CiviCRM's own Spark hosting lets you choose North America or Europe.
plans: Any host with UK or EU servers; Spark with the Europe option
ai_detail: Core CiviCRM has no supplier AI service that receives your data. Check any AI extensions or host services you add.
nonprofit_offer: Free open-source software (AGPL 3). You pay for hosting and support; Spark hosting starts at about USD 15 a month.
note: Where your data lives and whether two-factor login is available depend on your hosting partner and the website system CiviCRM runs on. Ask your host where the servers are and whether you can get a full database copy.

name: Donorfy
storage: EU by default (assumed plan: Starter). Hosted on Microsoft Azure North Europe in Dublin, Ireland. Enterprise can use private cloud hosting.
plans: All plans
ai_detail: Donorfy is being linked to The Access Group's Access Evo AI features. Access says Evo AI has zero data retention for training and inputs are never used to improve models. Evo features were switched on automatically from 17 November 2025 and admins can turn them off.
note: Data is held in Ireland. A full export with all fields and attachments costs extra, so ask for the price before you decide to leave.

name: HubSpot
storage: Set at sign-up by the IP address location (assumed plan: free CRM or Starter). HubSpot has an EU data centre in Germany; accounts started in the US data centre can be moved to the EU on any plan. HubSpot does not state where UK sign-ups go. Usage data and some processing still go to the US.
plans: All plans (EU data centre by sign-up location or migration)
ai_detail: HubSpot uses customer data such as CRM activity to train its models by default. Super Admins can switch off 'AI Model Training' under Settings > AI > Access. Opt-out applies from then on only. Accounts with Sensitive Data enabled are opted out.
nonprofit_offer: 40% off Professional and Enterprise for new annual customers, but HubSpot's page limits it to nonprofits registered in North America, Australia and New Zealand. Starter is excluded.
note: Check Account defaults to see which data centre your account uses, as UK sign-ups may land in the US. HubSpot trains AI on your CRM data unless a Super Admin switches it off.

name: ForeningLet
storage: EU only. ForeningLet's data processing agreement says processing takes place 'inden for EUs grænser' (within the EU) and that personal data is never transferred to third countries. Amazon (Ireland) hosts the IT infrastructure. The agreement does not name a country.
plans: Base package from 99 kr a month for up to 100 members, before VAT (checked 29 September 2026). The data processing terms apply to all customers.
ai_detail: ForeningLet has an AI assistant that searches the user guide and, depending on user rights, looks up members and invoices. The user guide says: 'Ingen data sendes videre til tredjepart' (no data is sent to third parties) and 'Al behandling kører på servere hos ForeningLet' (all processing runs on ForeningLet's servers). AI model training: unknown.
nonprofit_offer: Unknown.
note: ForeningLet offers a data processing agreement (databehandleraftale) and says data stays in the EU, hosted by Amazon in Ireland. It holds your members' personal data, so check that your organisation has accepted the agreement and that one person is not the only administrator. You can export member lists to Excel or CSV, so do that regularly. Two-factor login is available: an administrator switches it on under Opsætning, Forening, To-faktor-login, and it then applies to all administrators, with a one-time code sent by email.

name: Membersite
storage: Denmark. EG says its Membercare membership system, which includes the Membersite self-service portal, is 'udviklet, hostet og GDPR-sikret i Danmark' (developed, hosted and GDPR-secured in Denmark). The same page also says 'udviklet og hosted i norden' (Nordic), so the exact country is worth confirming.
plans: Membersite is the member self-service part of EG Membercare (packages Basis, Udvidet and Premium). Prices are not published. Plan assumed: any Membercare package.
ai_detail: Unknown. EG's Membercare page lists AI features on its roadmap for 2026 (Genie and Smart tekst, AI agents, churn predictions) but does not say whether customer data is used to train AI models.
note: Membersite was made by Groupcare, which EG bought in November 2023, and is now sold as part of EG Membercare. EG says the system is hosted in Denmark. EG's public pages do not show a data processing agreement (databehandleraftale) or a price for Membercare, so ask EG for both. Ask how you get your member data out if you leave, and whether administrators can use two-step login. Export terms, two-step login and AI training: unknown.

name: JustGiving
storage: Not stated. The privacy policy says some personal data may be stored outside the UK, EU or EEA, and JustGiving is covered by Blackbaud's EU-US Data Privacy Framework certification.
ai_detail: The privacy policy says JustGiving uses machine learning and analytics to make inferences about users (donors and fundraisers) to tailor content, and users can opt out. It does not say whether charity or donor data trains AI models. Charity account data: unknown.
nonprofit_offer: Built for charities. Start plan has no monthly fee; Grow plan is £15 or £39 a month plus VAT depending on income. No platform fee on donations; card processing 1.9% + 30p; 5% fee on Gift Aid claimed.
note: JustGiving and your charity are separate data controllers for donor data, so donors' details sit in JustGiving's own system as well as yours. It does not say where that data is stored, so ask Blackbaud if location matters to you.

name: Enthuse
storage: UK hosting on Microsoft Azure and AWS
plans: All plans
ai_detail: The privacy notice does not mention AI, machine learning or model training. Opt-out setting: unknown.
nonprofit_offer: Charity-only product. 0% platform fee; monthly subscriptions from £0 (mass participation) to £39.99; payment fee 1.9% + 30p; 5% Gift Aid fee.
note: Enthuse says it hosts in the UK and requires two-step verification for all admin users. Check which monthly package you are on, because features and fees differ by product.

name: Stripe
contracting_entity: Stripe Payments Europe, Ltd. (contracting entity for UK and EEA); Stripe Technology Company Limited (data controller outside the Americas)
storage: Transferred to the US (and India) by default. UK or EU storage option for ordinary accounts: unknown.
ai_detail: The privacy policy (updated April 2026) lists training AI models to power services and prevent fraud. Stripe's Payments Foundation Model is trained on tens of billions of transactions across its network. Specific opt-out for model training: unknown. Rights requests go through the Privacy Center.
nonprofit_offer: Discounted processing on request for registered nonprofits (UK included) where at least 80% of volume is donations. Tickets, memberships and registration fees do not count.
note: Stripe moves your payment and donor data to the US and uses transaction data to train its fraud and payments AI. Two-step login is optional, so an admin should switch on the setting that requires it for the whole team.

name: PayPal
contracting_entity: PayPal UK Ltd (UK accounts); PayPal Giving Fund UK is a separate registered charity (1110538)
storage: Stored in the US and other countries by PayPal's service providers
ai_detail: The UK privacy statement (28 October 2025) says personal data is used to improve services, including improving risk models and developing new products and features. It does not use the phrase AI training. Opt-out: unknown.
nonprofit_offer: Discounted charity rate on application for confirmed charities (change business type to Non-profit and submit documents). PayPal Giving Fund enrolment is free and charges no fees to charities or donors, though partner platforms may add fees.
note: Donations through PayPal Giving Fund go to that fund first, and you only get a donor's name and email if they chose to share them. PayPal stores data in the US.

name: GoCardless
storage: Main processing for European payments on servers in the EEA; some suppliers may transfer data outside the EEA
plans: All plans
ai_detail: GoCardless says its Success+ retry models are trained on millions of recurring payments it has processed, and Protect+ fraud models use data from billions of transactions on its network. The merchant privacy notice (July 2026) says data is used to improve services and for automated fraud decisions. Opt-out: unknown.
nonprofit_offer: Charity Pricing plan: 25% off standard transaction fees for registered charities. CICs, companies limited by guarantee without share capital, custom pricing and add-on fees are excluded.
note: GoCardless processes European payments in the EEA and you can move your Direct Debit mandates out through a bulk change. CICs do not qualify for the charity discount.

name: Mollie
contracting_entity: Mollie B.V. (Mollie UK Ltd for UK merchants)
storage: Not stated by Mollie. Its privacy statement says some processing by third parties may happen outside the EEA. A third-party profile says Mollie commits to storing payment data in European data centres.
ai_detail: The privacy statement (18 July 2026) lists developing, training, using and enhancing automated systems including AI models as a purpose. No opt-out described.
note: Mollie says it usually offers no discount for charities, and it does not state where it stores data. Mollie treats itself as a separate controller, not your processor, so there is no data processing agreement to sign.

name: Eventbrite
storage: US. Eventbrite says it physically stores personal data in the United States.
ai_detail: The privacy policy (15 September 2026) does not mention AI training. The organiser DPA says Eventbrite acts as an independent controller when it uses attendee data for research to improve products and give recommendations. No AI sub-processors listed.
nonprofit_offer: 50% off the Eventbrite Pro marketing plan for verified nonprofits (via Percent). Ticketing fees are not discounted.
note: Eventbrite stores attendee data in the US and can use it for its own product research and recommendations. Eventbrite was bought by Bending Spoons in March 2026, so review the terms again.

name: pretix (hosted)
storage: Germany, on servers in data centres run by German companies
plans: All hosted accounts
ai_detail: The privacy page says pretix does not share customer data with anyone and uses event data only to run ticket sales and calculate its fees. No AI training mentioned.
nonprofit_offer: Non-profit pricing on request: 2.0% per paid ticket instead of 2.5% (capped at €15 or £13), and 2,500 free tickets a year before free-ticket fees apply. pretix decides eligibility case by case.
note: pretix hosts all data in Germany and most of its code is open source, so you could run it yourself. Two-factor login is optional, so turn on the team setting that requires it.

name: Ticket Tailor
storage: EU, on AWS in Dublin (Ireland) and Paris (France)
plans: All accounts
ai_detail: The privacy policy does not mention AI or model training, and no AI sub-processors are listed. No explicit statement either way.
nonprofit_offer: 50% off Ticket Tailor fees for registered charities, on proof of status. The help centre says other not-for-profits get 20%.
note: Ticket Tailor stores data in Ireland and France, and registered charities can claim half-price fees. Card payments go through your own Stripe, PayPal or Square account, so check those separately.

name: Zettle by PayPal (PayPal Point of Sale)
storage: Unknown. The privacy policy does not say where data is stored. It says Zettle transfers data to service providers in the US and Australia under Standard Contractual Clauses, and shares data with PayPal Group companies.
plans: Plan assumed: standard UK pay-as-you-go (1.75% per card transaction, no monthly fee, reader from GBP 29 before VAT for new business users).
ai_detail: Unknown. The UK privacy policy does not mention AI or machine-learning training. It mentions automated decisions for credit assessment, fraud and risk.
note: Zettle is now branded PayPal Point of Sale, so look for either name on your account and invoices. The service is provided by PayPal UK Ltd, and the privacy policy does not say where data is stored. Two-step verification is always on: PayPal's help says 'It is not possible to disable 2-step verification on the PayPal Point of Sale account.' Export sales reports to PDF, Excel or raw-data Excel from my.zettle.com (not the app) before you close. The help pages describe sales and product reports only, so ask Zettle how to get your customer list and full product catalogue out.

name: SumUp
storage: SumUp says 'for our European business we store our personal data within the European Economic Area'. It may transfer data to group companies and providers outside the EEA and UK. The policy does not say whether this covers UK accounts.
plans: Plan assumed: pay-as-you-go (1.69% per in-person card payment, no monthly fee). Payments Plus is GBP 19 a month before VAT, as stated on the pricing page.
ai_detail: Unknown. The privacy policy mentions developing 'machine-learning risk assessment tools' for fraud prevention and risk management. It has no statement on training on customer data for other purposes.
note: SumUp says it stores European data in the EEA, not the UK, so check that the wording covers your UK account. Turn on 2-step authentication for the main login: it is optional and codes go by email or SMS. Sales reports export to CSV or Excel from the dashboard. SumUp does not publish a charity rate on its charity page, so ask before assuming one.

name: MobilePay (Box, MyShop, Donations)
storage: Unknown. The MobilePay privacy notice and the merchant terms do not say where data is stored. The data processing agreement allows sub-processors in third countries with safeguards, and the sub-processor list is available on request. Plan assumed: a business agreement for MyShop or Donations, and a private MobilePay profile for a Box.
plans: Box needs only a MobilePay profile: free to create and to collect the first 999 kr, then 19 kr is taken for each 1,000 kr paid in. MyShop and Donations need a business agreement. Donations cost 0.99% plus 1 kr per transaction before VAT (checked 2026-09-29).
ai_detail: Unknown. The merchant terms and privacy notice make no statement about AI training. Plan assumed: business agreement.
nonprofit_offer: Donations cost 0.79% plus 1 kr per transaction, instead of 0.99% plus 1 kr, for ISOBRO members (prices before VAT, checked 2026-09-29). There is no general non-profit price for MyShop or Box.
note: Ask about the databehandleraftale before you use it for donor data. The published agreement covers only Loyalty and Login. For payments, the merchant terms say you and Vipps MobilePay are each independent controllers. The business portal signs in with MitID, and an administrator adds each user, so name two administrators. A Box belongs to a person's MobilePay profile, not to your organisation, so it is a weak fit for a 45-person non-profit. Settlement and transaction reports download as PDF, Excel (XLSX) or CSV from the business portal; export of other data: unknown.

name: Betalingsservice
job: Collecting membership fees and regular payments by direct debit
storage: Denmark. The Betalingsservice privacy notice (March 2026) says 'personal data is processed in Denmark and may be transferred to other countries'. Mastercard's general privacy notice says data moves within the Mastercard group and may go to the USA and other countries, under binding corporate rules and similar safeguards. Plan assumed: a creditor agreement with a data supplier agreement.
plans: Unknown. Prices are in a separate price list on betalingsservice.dk. Banks also offer Betalingsservice on their own terms.
ai_detail: Unknown. The Betalingsservice privacy notice does not mention AI.
nonprofit_offer: Unknown.
note: No databehandleraftale is offered. Mastercard Payment Services says it is an independent controller for Betalingsservice, so 'there should be no data processing agreements for these products'. Check how your membership system or bank sends the data, as they may need their own agreement with you. Transactions are approved with MitID Erhverv. Before you rely on it, ask what you can export and how you would move members to another way of collecting. Export terms and two-step login: unknown.

name: WordPress.com
storage: US and EU. WordPress.com stores personal data on servers in both the US and the EU and cannot restrict a site to one location. Self-hosted WordPress is different: data lives wherever your web host puts it.
plans: Business plan sites can pick EU West as the primary data centre when hosting features are first activated, but data is still not restricted to the EU.
ai_detail: Automattic licenses public site content to third parties, including AI companies, unless you tick 'Prevent third-party sharing' under Settings, Reading. This applies to public content. Assumed plan: Personal or Premium.
note: WordPress.com shares public site content with AI companies unless you tick 'Prevent third-party sharing' in Settings, Reading. If your site is self-hosted WordPress, ask your web host where the server is.

name: Squarespace
storage: US. Squarespace's privacy policy refers to 'our servers in the US', and its data processing addendum lets it transfer your data to other countries, in particular the US. Customers outside the US contract with Squarespace Ireland Limited.
plans: Plan assumed: any paid plan (Basic, Core, Plus or Advanced). Squarespace does not describe a storage choice on any plan.
ai_detail: Unknown. Squarespace's terms and privacy policy do not say whether customer content is used to train AI models. The terms let it use your content to provide and improve the services. Its help page says you can ask known AI crawlers to exclude your site; this is off by default and 'doesn't retroactively remove content previously scraped'.
nonprofit_offer: Enter NONPROFIT at checkout for 10% off your first payment (Squarespace help article, Building a nonprofit site).
note: Your site and contact records are held in the US. Squarespace says it exports only some content: one blog with its posts, layout pages and text and image blocks. Store pages, product blocks, video and audio blocks, styling and custom CSS do not export. Check what you would need to rebuild before you choose it. Two-factor sign-in (passkey, authenticator app or text message) is switched on by each person for their own account, so check every contributor has done it.

name: Wix
contracting_entity: Wix.com Ltd. (Israel) and its affiliated companies
storage: Wix says it stores information in data centres in the United States and Ireland. It does not say which one holds your site, and it also uses group companies and processors worldwide.
plans: Plan assumed: any Wix Premium plan. Wix does not say the data location differs by plan.
ai_detail: Wix's Generative AI Policy lists 'User-generated content (such as images and page layouts)' as a data source for its AI models, under a 'License given to Wix in the Terms of Use'. The policy describes no opt-out. Plan assumed: any Wix Premium plan.
nonprofit_offer: 70% off a 2-year Wix Premium plan for one website, plus a free 1-year domain voucher, for TechSoup member charities in supported countries. One coupon every 2 years. It renews at the standard rate unless you cancel. Not for Wix Studio plans.
note: Wix keeps data in the US and Ireland and does not let you choose. Wix says it uses content you create on its platform, such as images and page layouts, to develop its AI models, and describes no opt-out, so read its Generative AI Policy before you upload personal data. Wix does not offer a full-site export, so export your contacts, products, orders and bookings as CSV files before you cancel. Wix says you can turn on 2-step verification for your account, but does not say which plans include it, so check your own account settings. Check your country is on TechSoup's list and that the discount renews at full price after two years.

name: Shopify
storage: Shopify does not say which country holds your shop data. Its data processing addendum says customer personal data may be transferred and processed in any country where Shopify, its affiliates or service providers are located, including Singapore and Canada.
plans: Plan assumed: Basic, Grow or Advanced. Shopify's help says requiring staff to sign in with a secure method is available only on Shopify Plus.
ai_detail: Shopify says it does not use any merchant's store-level data to power Shopify Magic for other merchants, but does not say whether your data trains its models. Separately, its terms say Shopify Network Intelligence uses your customer data alongside other merchants' data for Enhanced Services, and you can turn this off in your settings. Assumed plan: Basic, Grow or Advanced.
note: Shopify does not name a country for your shop data, so ask where orders and customer records are kept. You can export products, customers and orders as CSV files from the admin, but check whether your theme, pages and app data come with them. Check whether two-step sign-in is on for every staff account, and whether Shopify Network Intelligence is off if you want it off. Your contract is with Shopify International Limited, in Ireland.

name: Google Analytics 4
storage: Global Google data centres, with no residency option. Traffic from UK and EU devices is collected on UK or EU servers and IP addresses are discarded, but data is then forwarded to Analytics servers for processing.
ai_detail: GA has data sharing settings, including 'Google products & services', which lets Google use your data to improve Google products, and 'Modeling contributions & business insights'. These are chosen at sign-up and can be changed under Admin, Account settings. Google does not state clearly on the help page which are on by default. Assumed plan: free standard GA4 property.
note: Google Analytics sends data outside the UK and EU and keeps detailed data for 14 months at most. Check the data sharing settings in Admin and switch off any you do not need.

name: Plausible Analytics
storage: Germany. Visitor data is stored on Hetzner servers in Falkenstein, Germany, on EU-owned infrastructure.
plans: All cloud plans
ai_detail: Statement on AI training: unknown. Plausible's DPA says it processes visitor data only on the customer's documented instructions, and its data policy says data is not used for advertising, profiling or monetisation. Assumed plan: Starter or Growth cloud plan.
nonprofit_offer: 15% off Business plans on annual billing, plus 2 free months, for nonprofits. Apply by contacting Plausible for a code.
note: Plausible keeps your website statistics in Germany with an EU company. You can only export summary figures on normal plans, not raw visit logs.

name: Umami Cloud
storage: You pick US or European Union as the data region when you set up the account. It cannot be changed afterwards.
plans: All cloud plans, if EU is selected at account setup
ai_detail: The privacy policy says Umami does not sell or share personal information, but it says nothing about AI training. Assumed plan: Hobby (free) or Pro.
note: Choose European Union when you set up Umami Cloud, because the data region cannot be changed later. The company is based in the US.

name: Matomo Cloud
storage: Germany. Matomo Cloud is hosted on AWS in Frankfurt, with backups in Dublin.
plans: All Matomo Cloud plans
ai_detail: InnoCraft acts as processor under the Matomo Cloud DPA. AI training on customer analytics data: unknown. Matomo's website privacy policy says its AI providers receive only aggregated reports and may not train general-purpose models. Assumed plan: Business or entry Cloud plan.
nonprofit_offer: Eligible non-profits may receive a discount on request.
note: Matomo Cloud keeps your analytics in Germany. The company is in New Zealand, which the EU and UK treat as having adequate data protection.

name: SurveyMonkey
contracting_entity: SurveyMonkey Inc. (EU entity: SurveyMonkey Europe UC, Ireland)
storage: US by default on AWS. The EU data centre is only available to Enterprise customers.
plans: Enterprise only (per the International Data Center Overview updated 15 April 2025)
ai_detail: The privacy notice says SurveyMonkey uses de-identified response data to train its models, and sentiment analysis and other machine learning features are switched on for all accounts and cannot be turned off. No opt-out from de-identified training is described. Assumed plan: Team Advantage or individual Advantage.
nonprofit_offer: Discounts for eligible nonprofits upgrading from a free plan, at SurveyMonkey's discretion and varying by country.
note: On ordinary plans SurveyMonkey stores your surveys in the US, as the EU data centre is Enterprise only. Free accounts cannot export responses or use two-factor sign-in.

name: Typeform
storage: US by default. Typeform's main servers are on AWS in Virginia, USA. EU data hosting is only on Enterprise or Growth Custom plans.
plans: Enterprise and Growth Custom
ai_detail: Typeform's AI FAQ says none of its customers' data is used to train any model. AI-powered insights can be switched off in Admin settings. Assumed plan: Basic or Plus.
nonprofit_offer: NGO discount of 25% forever on monthly plans or 40% forever on yearly plans, by application.
note: Typeform is a Spanish company but stores your forms in the US unless you are on an Enterprise or Growth Custom plan.

name: Jotform
storage: US by default. You can switch to EU storage in account settings (or use eu.jotform.com); form data then moves to Google Cloud servers in Frankfurt, Germany.
plans: Offered as an account setting; Jotform does not say it is limited to any plan.
ai_detail: Jotform's AI policy says personal data is never used to train its AI, but 'data you include in the forms you create, such as in form fields, may be used to train our AI'. No opt-out is described. Assumed plan: Bronze or Silver.
nonprofit_offer: 50% off all annual plans for nonprofit organisations.
note: Jotform stores forms in the US unless you switch on EU storage in your account settings, so check the Data tab. Its AI policy allows form content to be used for AI training.

name: Tally
storage: EU. Tally says it is 'Made and hosted in the EU' and that all form data is encrypted and stored in Europe. Exact country: unknown.
plans: All plans. Two-factor sign-in: Tally's help page states no plan limit.
ai_detail: Unknown. Tally has no explicit statement on training AI models. Its DPA says it processes personal data only on the customer's documented instructions and not for other purposes. The privacy notice separately says Tally may use data you provide to improve the tool. Assumed plan: Free or Pro.
nonprofit_offer: 30% off Tally Pro forever for new Pro customers that are non-profits.
note: Tally is a Belgian company and stores form data in the EU. Tally offers two-factor sign-in with an authenticator app, which each person turns on in their own account settings, so check every user has done it. You can download form responses as CSV from the Submissions tab.

name: LimeSurvey Cloud
storage: You choose the server country when creating the instance: Germany, Finland, United Kingdom, USA, Canada or Australia. Data is then stored only in that country.
plans: All Cloud plans, by choosing Germany, Finland or UK at setup
ai_detail: Unknown. LimeSurvey's privacy notice and product pages do not mention AI training. Assumed plan: Basic or Expert Cloud plan.
nonprofit_offer: 30% discount for charitable organisations on proof of charity status.
note: When you create your LimeSurvey Cloud site, choose the UK, Germany or Finland as the server location. Two-factor sign-in is a built-in plugin you need to switch on.

name: Xero
storage: US by default. Xero says it hosts customer data with AWS on servers in the US, and some EU customer data is processed in New Zealand.
ai_detail: Xero says its JAX assistant does not use customer data to train the LLMs it uses, and its AWS, Azure and GCP model providers do not retain it. Separately, the UK privacy notice says Xero uses personal data to improve services and develop new products 'using AI/ML' and offers no specific opt-out. Assumed plan: Standard or Premium business plan.
nonprofit_offer: 25% off business pricing plans for registered not-for-profits, applied after Xero verifies charity status (claim within 31 days of subscribing).
note: Xero stores your accounts in the US, not the UK. Export your reports, CSV lists and attachments before you ever cancel, as there is no one-click full backup.

name: QuickBooks Online
storage: Not clearly stated. A UK help article says data is kept on AWS 'in your home country to satisfy data residency laws', but Intuit's UK GDPR page reserves the right to store and process data in the US and other countries.
ai_detail: Intuit's global privacy statement says it may use personal information to improve and develop products 'by training our artificial intelligence models and other machine learning models', and creates anonymised aggregate statistics. No specific opt-out is offered beyond general UK/EU data rights such as objecting to processing. Assumed plan: Simple Start or Essentials.
note: Intuit does not clearly say whether UK accounts are stored in the UK, and it trains its AI models on customer data. Ask Intuit in writing where your data is held if that matters to your trustees.

name: Sage Accounting
storage: Ireland. Sage lists AWS in Ireland as the data hosting location for Sage Business Cloud Accounting.
plans: All Sage Accounting plans
ai_detail: Sage's AI and data ethics principles say it analyses customer product data together with other customers' data 'to develop and train AI models', and that it does not offer a choice on use of anonymised data. Identifiable data is not shared with third parties without permission. Assumed plan: Sage Accounting Standard or Plus.
nonprofit_offer: Sage says registered charities, trusts and non-profits can save up to 50% through Sage Foundation. Check the offer is still live before relying on it.
note: Sage keeps your accounts in Ireland, inside the EU. Sage uses anonymised customer data to train its AI and there is no opt-out for that.

name: e-conomic
storage: EU. e-conomic says your accounting data is hosted in the EU with AWS. Its sub-processor list also names Google (Ireland) and Microsoft Azure (Netherlands and Ireland) for the database backup. The sub-processor list can include companies inside and outside the EU or EEA, so read the current list. Assumed plan: any e-conomic package.
plans: Packages are Basis, Plus, Smart and Komplet, from 249 to 649 kr a month before VAT (checked 2026-09-29). e-conomic does not say the hosting differs by package.
ai_detail: e-conomic's subscription terms let it use your application data 'to maintain, offer, price and develop the Application'. After the agreement ends it may use the data in anonymised form. The terms do not mention training AI models. Assumed plan: any e-conomic package.
nonprofit_offer: Unknown.
note: A databehandleraftale (data processing agreement) is offered on e-conomic's own site, and you can download it from the help centre. Export your data before you cancel. The terms say e-conomic may delete it after the agreement ends, and export is via CSV files. An archive licence keeps data for 5 years if you buy one. e-conomic's help centre says two-factor sign-in (2FA) is required to log in, and an admin can enforce it for all users on your agreement.

name: FreeAgent
storage: FreeAgent says it stores customer information 'in data centres located in Ireland across multiple availability zones'. Its Trust Centre says the UK, so check which applies to you. Its subprocessor list also names AWS, Google Cloud and DigitalOcean with locations in the US, UK and EU.
plans: Plan assumed: any FreeAgent plan (sole trader, partnership, limited company or landlord). No plan difference is stated.
ai_detail: Unknown. FreeAgent's Trust Centre says it has internal policies and controls for AI, and no AI or LLM provider appears in its subprocessor list. Its privacy notice does not mention AI. There is no statement on training on customer data.
nonprofit_offer: 50% off FreeAgent subscription costs for registered charities. Not applied automatically: contact FreeAgent support with your charity number. Not-for-profits, CICs and social enterprises are considered case by case. It does not apply to purchased add-ons (FreeAgent help article, Choosing the appropriate business type for a charity).
note: FreeAgent stores your accounts in Ireland (its Trust Centre says UK). 2-step verification is optional and uses an authenticator app, so switch it on for every user. Use Export All Data to take a full copy with attachments before you ever cancel. FreeAgent offers registered charities 50% off, but you have to ask support for it. FreeAgent is owned by NatWest Group and is free with some NatWest business accounts, so check what happens to your plan if you close that account.

name: Dinero
storage: Netherlands, with a copy in Ireland. Dinero says it is hosted in the cloud with Google and Microsoft Azure, with files and data physically on servers in the Netherlands, and uploaded files also mirrored on servers in Ireland. Its sub-processor list also names some US-based suppliers (for example Mailchimp and Datadog) and says it uses EU standard contractual clauses where a supplier is outside the EU. Assumed plan: any Dinero plan.
plans: Starter (free, up to 100,000 kr yearly revenue), Starter+, Pro and Total, from 245 to 545 kr a month (checked 2026-09-29). Whether those prices include VAT: unknown. Dinero's pages do not say the hosting differs by plan.
ai_detail: Dinero's terms let it use your application data 'to maintain, offer, price and develop the Application', and after the user relationship ends only in anonymised form. The terms do not mention training AI models. Dinero's sub-processor list names Microsoft Azure as host of 'databases and AI models' and Visma's SmartScan for reading invoice data. Assumed plan: any Dinero plan.
nonprofit_offer: No non-profit discount is listed. Dinero says Dinero Starter (free up to 100,000 kr yearly revenue) can be used by associations, and it has a version set up for associations.
note: A databehandleraftale is offered. Dinero says it takes effect when you register as a customer, and that continued use after an update counts as acceptance. Two-factor login can be switched on, but Dinero does not say who must use it or on which plan, so check each user has it. Export: postings, account statements and reports download as CSV or PDF, a SAF-T file is available, and contacts and products export as CSV. The paid backup file (495 kr before VAT) holds reports, sales invoices and credit notes, postings and all uploaded bilag that have been posted, as PDF and CSV, one financial year at a time. Dinero says it keeps accounting data for five years after you cancel.

name: Billy (now Shine Regnskab)
storage: EU. Shine's privacy policy says your data is kept on servers with Google Cloud and Amazon Web Services inside the EU, but some data is also passed outside the EU, including to the USA. Its data processing agreement lists Amazon (Luxembourg) and Google (Ireland) and some US suppliers such as Stripe, Intercom and Datadog. Assumed plan: any Billy or Shine Regnskab plan.
plans: Free (3 invoices and 10 expense receipts a month), Basic, Plus and Complete. Billy's price page and Shine's page show different prices for the same plans, so check the price at sign-up. Billy's pages do not say the hosting differs by plan.
ai_detail: Shine's privacy policy says your data is not used 'for developing, training or improving AI technologies, except when strictly necessary to deliver our services'. This is the Shine policy, not a Billy-only one. Its terms also let Shine use content you submit without compensation. Assumed plan: any plan.
nonprofit_offer: No non-profit discount is listed on Billy's pricing pages or in its article on accounting for non-profits.
note: Billy is now run under the Shine name, and billy.dk pages for the data processing agreement and terms send you to Shine's pages. A databehandleraftale is offered and counts as signed when you accept the terms. Export before you cancel: the older Billy terms say you must do the export yourself before the subscription ends. Billy's backup is a zip file with a folder for each transaction, converted to PDF with its attachments. Lists such as the posting journal, contacts, products and chart of accounts export separately (CSV, Excel or PDF), so export those too. Two-factor login: unknown, so ask Shine whether it is available on your plan. Check who the contracting company is on your invoice, as the privacy policy names a different company from the terms.

name: 1Password
storage: Depends on the sign-up site: accounts made on 1Password.eu are hosted in the EU, 1Password.com in the US. Data is never moved automatically between regions.
plans: All plans; choose 1Password.eu when creating the account
ai_detail: Vault items are end-to-end encrypted and 1Password staff cannot read them. The privacy notice does not describe using customer data to train AI.
nonprofit_offer: Discounts for eligible nonprofits through the sales team; no published rate.
note: Make sure your account address ends in 1Password.eu if you want EU hosting, because an account made on 1Password.com is in the US and cannot be moved without starting again.

name: Bitwarden
storage: You pick US or EU in the server drop-down when you create the account or organisation. EU data sits in Microsoft Azure in the EU.
plans: All cloud plans; choose the EU server at sign-up
ai_detail: Vault data is encrypted on the device before it reaches Bitwarden's servers, so it cannot be read for training. No AI training use is described.
note: Choose the EU server when you sign up, because moving from US to EU later means exporting and re-importing everything. Most of the code is open source under GPL and AGPL, with some business features under Bitwarden's own licence.

name: LastPass
parent: Francisco Partners and Elliott Investment Management (private equity owners)
storage: US by default. LastPass also runs vault storage in Europe (Ireland, Germany, UK), used when elected at account creation.
plans: Not stated by plan; region is elected when the account is created
ai_detail: Vault contents are encrypted on the device and LastPass says it cannot read them. The privacy policy does not mention AI training for account or usage data.
note: Vaults are stored in the US unless Europe was chosen when the account was set up, so ask LastPass which region yours uses. LastPass had a major breach in 2022 that led to a UK ICO fine in 2025.

name: Proton Pass
storage: Proton-owned servers located only in Switzerland, Germany or Norway. Proton does not say which country a given account uses and there is no customer choice.
ai_detail: Proton Pass data, including metadata, is end-to-end encrypted and Proton says it cannot decrypt it.
nonprofit_offer: Discounted rates for nonprofits on Proton Pass and other Proton services; rate not published.
note: Your vault may be stored in Switzerland or Norway rather than the EU, although Switzerland and Norway have strong data protection laws. Business plans let admins require two-factor sign-in for everyone.

name: KeePassXC
storage: On the user's own device, in an encrypted .kdbx file. It only goes elsewhere if you put the file in a cloud folder you choose.
ai_detail: The app runs locally and the project says no stored data is ever sent to it or third parties.
nonprofit_offer: Free for everyone.
note: KeePassXC keeps passwords in a file on your own computer, so data location is wherever you save or sync that file. Decide where it is stored and backed up, and who holds the master password. It has no two-step sign-in in the usual sense: it uses a master password, with an optional key file or hardware key. Answer Yes to two-step sign-in only if you use one of those.

name: Trello
storage: US (AWS data centres). Trello is not listed among Atlassian products that offer data residency.
ai_detail: Atlassian's data contribution scheme, in force from 17 August 2026, uses metadata and in-app data from Free and Standard plans of Jira, Confluence and JSM for AI by default. Atlassian says it does not apply to Trello because Trello has no data contribution settings. Recheck if Trello gets these settings.
nonprofit_offer: Atlassian Social Impact licence: 75% off Trello Standard, Premium and Enterprise for eligible nonprofits.
note: Trello data is held in the US and there is no option to move it to the UK or EU. Export each board to JSON from time to time, as spreadsheet and full workspace exports need Premium.

name: Asana
storage: US (Virginia) by default. Frankfurt storage is a paid add-on on Enterprise and included in Enterprise+.
plans: Enterprise (paid add-on) and Enterprise+; region Frankfurt, Germany; no UK region
ai_detail: Asana states it does not use customer data for training and its AI partners are contractually barred from doing so. Admins can switch AI features off in the admin console.
nonprofit_offer: Asana for Nonprofits: 50% off Starter and Advanced plans for eligible registered nonprofits, including outside the US.
note: Asana keeps your data in the US unless you pay for Enterprise with the EU add-on. Only Enterprise plans can force everyone to use two-factor sign-in, so ask staff to turn it on themselves.

name: Notion
storage: US by default. Enterprise customers can choose Frankfurt (EU) for workspace content at no extra cost.
plans: Enterprise only; EU region Frankfurt; no UK region; Notion Mail and Calendar excluded
ai_detail: Notion says it does not use workspace data to train models by default. Sharing is only through the opt-in AI LEAP programme. AI subprocessors are contractually barred from training on customer data.
nonprofit_offer: 50% off the Business plan for eligible nonprofits worldwide (up to three workspaces), after verification.
note: On non-Enterprise plans your Notion content is stored in the US. Two-step sign-in is available to everyone but admins cannot enforce it for members, so ask each person to switch it on.

name: Airtable
storage: US by default. EU storage is only available on Enterprise Scale, and some metadata and login data stay in the US even then.
plans: Enterprise Scale only; EU region; no UK region
ai_detail: Airtable's AI Terms say it will not use or let AI providers use customer data to train generative AI models. On Free, Team and similar plans, providers may keep inputs for up to 30 days for safety checks.
nonprofit_offer: 50% off the Team plan for eligible registered nonprofits, including outside the US; monthly billing only; not for Business or Enterprise Scale.
note: Airtable stores your bases in the US on the Team plan. Leaving is hard because export is one table at a time as CSV, so keep regular copies and save attachments separately.

name: monday.com
storage: Set by where the first user is when the account opens. Accounts opened from the EU on Standard, Pro or Enterprise go to the EU region (Germany); the UK is not named, and most others default to the US.
plans: Standard and Pro accounts created on or after 23 January 2023, and Enterprise; not Free or Basic
ai_detail: monday.com says it does not use customer data to train AI models and bars its AI providers from doing so. It may access data temporarily, up to 60 days, to improve services and detect abuse; an admin can opt out by emailing ai-support@monday.com.
nonprofit_offer: 10 free seats on the Pro plan for eligible nonprofits, 70% off extra seats and Pro add-ons, 33% off Enterprise; UK Community Interest Companies are excluded.
note: Check Administration, then Profile, to see which region your account is stored in, because it is fixed when the account is created and cannot be moved later. UK charities should not assume EU storage.

name: OpenProject (cloud)
storage: EU. The standard cloud runs on Amazon Web Services with all services in Europe; hosting on EU-owned Scaleway is available on request.
plans: All cloud plans
ai_detail: OpenProject does not run its own AI model. AI use is through its MCP server with a client and model the organisation chooses. Its privacy pages do not mention AI training.
nonprofit_offer: Special rates for NGOs and educational institutions on request from sales; no published discount.
note: Your data stays in the EU, but on a US-owned cloud provider unless you ask for EU-owned Scaleway hosting. Check backup size, as attachments over 1 GB are left out of self-service backups.

name: Zapier
job: Connecting tools and moving data between them
storage: US. Zapier says it is hosted on Amazon Web Services in the United States. Zapier also passes your data between the other tools you connect, and each of those tools keeps its own copy.
plans: Plan assumed: Free, Professional or Team. Enterprise differs on AI training and audit log length.
ai_detail: Zapier says: 'Enterprise customers are automatically opted out of data training. Customers on other plans can opt out by filling out the opt-out form.' So on Free, Professional and Team, opting out is your step. Checked 29 September 2026.
nonprofit_offer: 15% off any paid plan (not pay-per-task charges) for non-profits, after Zapier checks your charitable status. Its pages do not say whether UK charities are covered, so check.
note: Zapier moves data between your other tools, such as forms, email lists and accounts, and passes it through US servers on the way. List which tools each Zap touches, and check the settings of each one. Unless you are on Enterprise, fill in Zapier's opt-out form if you do not want your content used for AI training. You can export your Zaps and account data, but exporting Zaps is only for Team and Enterprise plans.

name: Canva
storage: US by default. EU storage for designs and media is only offered on Enterprise, Campus and District plans.
plans: Enterprise (and Campus, District education plans); no UK option
ai_detail: Canva says it does not use content to improve AI unless privacy settings allow it, and the default is off. Individual users can opt in or out in Privacy settings. Teams, Business and Enterprise accounts currently cannot opt in. Canva for Nonprofits runs as a team account.
nonprofit_offer: Canva for Nonprofits: free Canva Pro and team features for up to 50 people for eligible registered charities; extra seats at 50% off Enterprise pricing.
note: Your designs are stored in the US on the Nonprofits plan, and EU storage is only available on Enterprise. Download important designs as PDF or PPTX regularly, because there is no editable export.

name: Adobe Creative Cloud
job: Design, photo and print (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign)
storage: Plan assumed: Creative Cloud for teams. Adobe's help pages say cloud storage data centres are in Dublin (Ireland) for the EU region, Virginia (US) and Tokyo, and that for organisations with Adobe storage for business in the EU, storage is aligned to the EU region. Adobe's pages name the EU but not the UK. Adobe's privacy policy says its main processing locations for personal information are the US and India.
plans: Creative Cloud for teams (business storage, 1 TB per user, shared across the team). Region is set by the organisation's country, not chosen by you. Whether a UK organisation is placed in the EU region: unknown. Teams pricing: unknown.
ai_detail: Adobe says it does not train Firefly on subscribers' personal content: 'No, Adobe does not train Adobe Firefly models or partner models on any Creative Cloud subscribers' personal content.' Separately, Adobe's content analysis setting lets Adobe analyse content stored on its servers to improve products; individuals can turn it off in their privacy settings. What applies to teams accounts is unknown, and an Adobe community thread reports there is no admin switch to turn it off for a whole team. Plan assumed: Creative Cloud for teams.
nonprofit_offer: Adobe for Nonprofits (UK page): discounted Creative Cloud is for individual memberships, run through TechSoup. TechSoup lists the Creative Cloud for education (teams) discount as no longer available. No nonprofit discount is listed for Creative Cloud for teams. Teams prices: unknown.
note: Export: you can download files from the Creative Cloud desktop app or adobe.com/files, export a whole Libraries collection from the desktop app, and save or export work from Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign as PDF, PNG, JPEG, SVG, TIFF and PSD. Cloud documents use Adobe's own .psdc format and need opening in Photoshop to save as PSD or other formats. Bulk download on the web is limited, so use the desktop app for large libraries. When a teams licence is cancelled, storage for that licence drops to 5 GB and Adobe says you have 30 days to move anything above that out, after which some or all files may be removed. Check with your Adobe admin whether the content analysis setting is on for your team, and ask Adobe in writing which region your team's files are stored in, because Adobe's pages name the EU but not the UK. Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign files also live on each person's computer unless saved to the cloud, so check where your team saves them. Nonprofit discounts apply to individual memberships through TechSoup, so a small team may not qualify for a teams discount. Adobe offers a data processing addendum for business customers: ask for it. Teams pricing: unknown.

name: Figma
storage: US by default. Figma's privacy policy says 'All personal information we process is transferred to, processed and stored in the United States, where our headquarters and our main servers are located.' Local file hosting (EU and other regions) is only on the Enterprise plan. Billing information, metadata, logs and file search data stay outside that option.
plans: Enterprise only (localised file hosting, EU among the regions). Plan assumed for the rest: Professional. No UK region listed.
