ai_detail: Figma's help centre says content training is on by default for Starter and Professional teams, and off for Organisation and Enterprise plans: 'By default, content training is turned on for Professional teams.' Team admins can turn it off on Starter and Professional. On Organisation and Enterprise it is currently disabled and cannot be switched on. Plan assumed: Professional.
nonprofit_offer: Figma says it has no nonprofit discount: 'We do not have any discounts for non-profits. Anyone is welcome to use Figma's free plan.' Students and educators can get the Education plan free. Professional Full seat is listed at USD 16 a month (US dollars; the page does not say whether VAT is added).
note: On the Starter and Professional plans, content training is switched on by default, so a team admin should check the setting and switch it off if you do not want your files used. Files are stored in the US unless you are on Enterprise. Two-step verification is available on any plan but each person sets it up, and only Enterprise with Governance+ lets an admin require it. You can save a local .fig copy of each file, which works in Figma only.

name: Affinity (by Canva)
contracting_entity: Canva UK Operations Ltd for UK billing addresses; Canva Pty Ltd (Australia) for most other countries, including Ireland and Denmark
storage: Your design files are stored on your own device and the supplier says it cannot access them. A Canva account is needed to download and activate the app. Anything you upload or export to Canva sits in your Canva account, and Affinity does not say where that is held.
plans: Plan assumed: the free Affinity app with a free Canva account. AI tools need a paid Canva plan.
ai_detail: The supplier says content in Affinity is not used to train AI features. The Canva AI tools inside Affinity need a paid Canva plan and an internet connection, and content you upload or export to Canva follows your Canva privacy settings.
nonprofit_offer: Free for individuals. Whether Canva for Nonprofits terms apply to Affinity: unknown.
note: Affinity keeps files on your computer, but you need a Canva account to get and activate it. Check who in your organisation owns that Canva account, and whether you turn on two-step sign-in for it (the Affinity pages do not say). Export: Affinity's help lists PNG, JPEG, GIF, TIFF, PSD, PDF, SVG, EPS, EXR and HDR. Your working files use Affinity's own .af format, so export a copy in a standard format for anything you need to keep long term. If anyone uses the paid AI tools or exports to Canva, check the Canva privacy settings for that content.

name: GIMP
contracting_entity: GIMP team (community project). Donations are handled by the GNOME Foundation as fiscal agent.
storage: On your own device, in the files you save. It only goes elsewhere if you save or share those files to a cloud folder or service you choose.
ai_detail: The app runs on your device and the project says it does not collect, transmit, share or use any personal data. It checks for new versions no more than once a week in some builds.
nonprofit_offer: Free for everyone.
note: GIMP has no account and no sign-in, so there is no two-step sign-in to switch on. Your images live wherever you save them, so decide where they are stored and backed up. The project says it collects no personal data, apart from a weekly update check in some builds. The US location is the GNOME Foundation that handles GIMP's donations, not a place where your data is held. Export: GIMP saves in its own XCF format, which 'is the only format that can store everything about an image', and exports to a wide variety of formats through File, then Export As (including PNG, JPEG and TIFF; it opens Photoshop PSD files). Keep an XCF copy for editing and an export for sharing.

name: Inkscape
contracting_entity: Inkscape project, a member project of Software Freedom Conservancy (US non-profit)
storage: On your own device, in the files you save. It only goes elsewhere if you save or share those files to a cloud folder or service you choose.
ai_detail: The app runs on your device and the project's privacy policy says the software does not collect or transmit any personal information.
nonprofit_offer: Free for everyone.
note: Inkscape has no account and no sign-in, so there is no two-step sign-in to switch on. Your logos and drawings live wherever you save them, so decide where they are stored and backed up. Inkscape saves in SVG, an open standard that many other programs can read, and exports to PNG, PDF, EPS and other formats, so you can take your files with you. The US location is the Software Freedom Conservancy, which is the project's legal home, not a place where your data is held.

name: BrightPay
storage: Bright says its data is 'hosted in European regions', 'in EU/Ireland or UK ISO 27001 certified datacentres', and lists Microsoft Azure, AWS, OVH and Google as hosts. Its support desk (Zendesk) and email delivery (Twilio SendGrid) are in the US.
plans: Plan assumed: BrightPay cloud. Bright says only the cloud version is offered for 2026/27, and BrightPay for Windows was discontinued after 5 April 2026. Price depends on the number of employers and employees, and Bright points to a pricing calculator; monthly or annual billing is offered. Fixed price: unknown.
ai_detail: Unknown. Bright's subprocessor list names no AI provider.
note: BrightPay holds payroll and employee data, so ask Bright where your cloud data sits: it says Ireland, UK or EU, not one country. Two-factor sign-in is optional, and an owner or administrator can make it compulsory for every user. Bright's cloud FAQ says you cannot save a file of your payroll data to your computer, but reports can be downloaded as CSV or PDF, so save your reports after each pay run. If you still use desktop BrightPay, check your backup is on your own storage, as that version has ended.

name: Sage Payroll
storage: Sage's list of sub-processors names Amazon Web Services (a US company) for data hosting and cloud infrastructure for its payroll products, with hosting and processing in Ireland. Plan: cloud Sage Payroll. The list is dated 2023 on one copy, so ask Sage to confirm the current location in writing.
plans: Plan assumed: cloud Sage Payroll (Essentials, Standard or Premium). Sage 50 Payroll on your own computer is a different product and is not covered.
ai_detail: Unknown for Sage Payroll specifically. Sage's general AI and data ethics page says it analyses product data together with data from other Sage customers to develop and train AI models, where the law allows. Ask Sage whether this applies to your payroll data and whether you can opt out.
note: Payroll holds names, addresses, National Insurance numbers, pay and bank details, so ask Sage in writing which company you contract with and whether your data is used to train AI. Sage's help says cloud Sage Payroll cannot export all your payroll data at once or take a backup, so run and save your reports (the detailed pay run report can be saved as CSV) after each pay run. Check whether two-step sign-in is switched on for every payroll user; which plans have it is unknown.

name: BrightHR
storage: UK for customers who subscribe in the UK. BrightHR says it stores data in the country of subscription, on Microsoft Azure. Irish subscribers' data is kept in the EU.
plans: Plan assumed: any UK subscription (Core HR Software, Enhanced HR Support or Full HR, Health & Safety and Wellbeing). BrightHR does not tie the storage location to a plan.
ai_detail: Unknown. BrightHR's security page says nothing about using customer data to train AI.
note: Staff records, absence and documents are kept in the UK when you subscribe in the UK. BrightHR says you can export data at any time through reports (Employees, Absence, Documents), downloaded as CSV or Excel, but it does not describe a single full export, so ask what you would receive on leaving. Two-factor sign-in is available: each user turns it on in My Account using an authenticator app. Which plans have it, and whether an administrator can require it for everyone, is unknown, so check your admin settings. Contracts run for 24, 36 or 60 months, so check the length and the notice terms before you sign.

name: Breathe HR
contracting_entity: Centurion Management Systems Ltd (trading as Breathe)
storage: UK. Breathe says it uses the AWS London region (eu-west-2), with a failover centre elsewhere in the UK, and that none of your data leaves the UK.
plans: All plans (Micro, Starter, Regular, Pro, Premium, Plus). Breathe does not state a plan condition on where data is kept.
ai_detail: Unknown. Breathe says it holds ISO 42001 (AI management) certification and that aggregated usage data is redacted before it reaches its business intelligence system, but it does not state whether customer data is used to train AI models.
note: Staff records are kept in London on Amazon Web Services. Breathe says you can export employee data and download documents yourself. Its help says two-factor sign-in is on for Admin accounts, and from 25 August 2026 it is being switched on for HR accounts in batches, so check it is on for everyone who can see staff records. Breathe is owned by an Australian company, ELMO, so check which entity is named on your order.

name: Google Ads (including Google Ad Grants)
contracting_entity: Google Ireland Limited (advertisers in Europe, the Middle East and Africa)
storage: Unknown. Google's data processing terms say it "may process Customer Personal Data in any country in which Google or its Subprocessors maintain facilities". Google lists its data centre locations publicly.
plans: Plan assumed: a standard Google Ads account, and the Google Ad Grants account for eligible charities. Google does not say the data location differs.
ai_detail: Unknown.
nonprofit_offer: Google Ad Grants: up to USD 10,000 a month in search ads on Google.com for qualifying non-profits. Your organisation must hold valid charity status in your country and be verified through Google for Nonprofits first.
note: Google Ads does not tell you one place your data is kept, so check the data processing terms for your account. You can download reports and account data as CSV and other files. Ad Grants is search ads only, and you apply through Google for Nonprofits first. Google says it "strongly encourages all advertisers to use 2-Step Verification" but does not make it a requirement on ordinary Ads accounts, so turn it on for every user.

name: Facebook Page
contracting_entity: Meta Platforms Ireland Limited (controller for people in the UK and EEA)
storage: Unknown. Plan assumed: a free Facebook Page. Meta's privacy policy says it shares information across its offices and data centres worldwide, and relies on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework for European data sent to Meta Platforms, Inc. in the US. Where a Page's posts or Messenger inbox are kept: unknown.
ai_detail: Meta says it uses public posts and comments from adult users' accounts on Facebook and Instagram to improve its generative AI models, and that it does not use private messages with friends and family (UK announcement, 13 September 2024; EU announcement, 14 April 2025). UK and EU users can send an objection form. Whether a Page's public posts count: unknown.
note: Facebook Pages are run through people's own Facebook logins, so check who holds full control. Aim for at least two trusted people, each with two-step login switched on and recovery details they can still reach. Meta says a Page with nobody holding full control is deactivated and scheduled for deletion. Messenger messages from supporters sit in the Page inbox. Meta's help centre offers a Page download (posts, photos, videos, Page information) and an Insights export. Whether the Messenger inbox is included: unknown. Test a download before you rely on it.

name: Instagram (professional account)
job: Organisation account, posts and direct messages
contracting_entity: Meta Platforms Ireland Limited (controller for people in the UK and EEA)
storage: Unknown. Plan assumed: a free professional (business or creator) account. Meta's privacy policy covers Instagram and says it shares information across its offices and data centres worldwide. Where an account's posts or direct messages are kept: unknown.
ai_detail: Meta says it uses public posts and comments from adult users' accounts on Facebook and Instagram to improve its generative AI models, and that it does not use private messages with friends and family (UK announcement, 13 September 2024; EU announcement, 14 April 2025). UK and EU users can send an objection form. Whether a professional account counts: unknown.
note: An Instagram professional account is still tied to one login. Check who knows the password, which email address and phone number are on it for recovery, and whether two-step login is on. If you connect it to a Facebook Page or a Business Portfolio, check who holds admin access there, because switching the account back to personal disconnects the Page and removes access to ads tools. Instagram's Export your information tool lets you download a profile's data. Whether direct messages are included: unknown, so test an export before you rely on it.

name: LinkedIn Company Page
contracting_entity: LinkedIn Ireland Unlimited Company (controller for people in the UK and EEA)
storage: Unknown. Plan assumed: a free LinkedIn Page. LinkedIn's privacy policy says it processes data both inside and outside the United States and uses legal mechanisms for transfers. Where a Page's content is kept: unknown.
ai_detail: LinkedIn says that from 3 November 2025 it uses some data from members in the EU, EEA, Switzerland, UK, Canada and Hong Kong to train content-generating AI models. It names profile details and public content members post, and says it does not include private messages. Members can turn this off in their own settings (Data for Generative AI Improvement). The setting belongs to each member's account, not to the Page.
note: A LinkedIn Page is managed by people's personal LinkedIn profiles. LinkedIn says every Page needs at least one super admin, so check that at least two trusted people hold that role, and that each has two-step verification on and can recover their own login. If the only admin leaves, other people have to request access and current super admins must approve it. LinkedIn says you can "create and export reports for analytics on visitors, content, followers, and competitors" as an XLS file. Export of follower lists and Page messages: unknown, so check what you can take out before you depend on it.

name: Meta Business Suite (Business Portfolio)
job: Admin layer over Facebook Pages, Instagram accounts and ads
contracting_entity: Meta Platforms Ireland Limited (controller for people in the UK and EEA)
storage: Unknown. Plan assumed: the free Meta Business Suite with a Business Portfolio. Meta's Data Processing Terms, which cover its business tools, say Meta may use sub-processors based in the USA, the EU or EEA, or other countries, and do not name where data is processed.
ai_detail: Unknown. Meta's generative AI statements (UK, 13 September 2024; EU, 14 April 2025) are about public posts from adult users' Facebook and Instagram accounts. Whether they apply to Business Portfolio or Business Suite data: unknown.
note: A Business Portfolio is only as safe as the personal Facebook logins behind it. Check who has full control, and that at least two trusted people do. Meta says two-factor authentication is required for some portfolios more than 90 days old, and that only people with full control can require it for everyone. Check your Pages and Instagram account are added to the portfolio, not only to one person's profile. Deleting a portfolio moves its Pages back to a personal profile. Insights can be exported (CSV, PDF or PNG). The portfolio's settings and people list have no export, so note them down.

name: X (formerly Twitter)
job: Organisation account, posts and direct messages
contracting_entity: X Internet Unlimited Company, Ireland (named Twitter International Unlimited Company in earlier terms; controller for people in the UK, EU and EFTA states). Parent company: unknown.
storage: Plan assumed: a free X account. Where an account's posts and messages are kept: unknown. X's global operations help page says information may be transferred to and stored in the United States, Ireland and other countries, and that X uses Standard Contractual Clauses where they apply.
ai_detail: X's privacy policy says X may share public posts and how you interact with Grok with xAI. X's Grok help page describes a setting under Privacy and safety, Data sharing and personalization, Grok & Third-party Collaborators, to allow or stop your public data and Grok interactions being used for training and fine-tuning. The setting is per account and does not remove data already collected. Privacy policy dated 15 July 2026. Updated Terms of Service take effect 9 October 2026, so check them again after that date.
note: X's terms say the contract for people in the UK, EU and EFTA states is with an Irish company. Parent company: unknown. Check who holds the login: X has a Delegate feature that lets people act for an account with an Admin or Contributor role, without sharing the password. Set it up so at least two trusted people can get in, then turn on two-step login for the main account. Authenticator app and security key are open to everyone; text message codes are for Premium subscribers only, so check which method you are using. You can download an archive of your data (profile, posts, direct messages, media, followers and lists, in HTML and JSON files) from Settings; ask for it before you need it. Check the Grok data-sharing setting on the account, and read the new terms before they start on 9 October 2026. Confirm the Delegate rules and the setting names in the account itself.

name: Bluesky
contracting_entity: Bluesky Social, PBC (controller; representatives named for the UK and EEA). Parent company: unknown.
storage: Plan assumed: a free Bluesky account on the Bluesky-run server. Country where an account is kept: unknown. Bluesky's privacy policy says: "We may transfer, process, and store all personal information we collect anywhere in the world." It relies on Standard Contractual Clauses for transfers out of the EEA, UK and Switzerland.
ai_detail: Bluesky's privacy policy and terms (both last updated 14 August 2025) do not mention training AI on your content; the policy mentions machine learning only for age checks. In a post on its own account on 15 November 2024, Bluesky said: 'We do not use any of your content to train generative AI, and have no intention of doing so.' That is a public statement, not a term of the contract, so check it again at each review. Posts, likes, follows and blocks are public by design on the network, so other people and companies can collect them. Recorded as No on Paul's decision of 30 September 2026, based on Bluesky's own public statement.
note: Bluesky is built on the AT Protocol, which is open source (MIT and Apache 2.0). Anyone can run their own server for an account (a PDS), and an account can move from one server to another, so exit is possible. The move needs care: it needs proof of control of the account, big accounts can hit errors and upload limits, and the guide is written for technical people. You can export your public records from Settings as a CAR file. The file does not hold images or private data; images are downloaded separately through the API, one by one. Two-step login by email code is available. App passwords let a scheduling tool sign in without your main password. Check who holds the password: no team or shared-access feature is documented, so at least two trusted people may need to know the login, kept in a shared password manager. Organisations can apply for a verification badge through Bluesky's form; ask if it is right for you. The promise not to train AI is a public post, not a term of the contract, and your posts are public, so check the AI position yourself.

name: Laptops on Windows 10
note: Free security updates ended on 14 October 2025. Paid extended updates cost US$61 per device for the year to 13 October 2026, then double.

name: Staff's own laptops or phones
note: Personal devices used for work are hard to secure, and hard to wipe when someone leaves.
